subject: chemistry
title: Oxygen in air and combustion of elements
key_idea: About 21% of air by volume is oxygen. It can be found by removing the oxygen with a reactive metal and measuring the volume lost. Magnesium, hydrogen and sulfur burn in oxygen to make oxides. Many metal carbonates give carbon dioxide when heated.

sections.heading: The percentage of oxygen in air

blocks.text: The percentage of oxygen in air is found by using up the oxygen in a fixed volume of air and measuring how much gas is lost.

items: Wet iron powder is put in a conical flask joined to a gas syringe holding a known volume of air.
The iron reacts with oxygen and water, so it rusts. Rust is brown hydrated iron(III) oxide.
Leave the apparatus until the volume of gas in the syringe stops changing.
Air is passed back and forth over heated copper powder between two syringes.
The copper reacts with oxygen to form black copper(II) oxide: 2Cu + O₂ → 2CuO.
Powder is used because it has a large surface area, so it reacts faster.
Let the gas cool before reading its volume, because a gas expands when it is hot.

blocks.text: A non-metal such as phosphorus can be used in the same way. The idea is the same: a substance reacts with the oxygen and the volume falls.

blocks.formula: % oxygen = (volume of oxygen used ÷ starting volume of air) × 100
blocks.label: Percentage of oxygen in air
where: volume of oxygen used = start volume − end volume of gas in the syringe
starting volume of air = syringe volume + volume of flask and tube, all in cm³

diagram.alt: Practise calculating the percentage of oxygen in air from gas syringe readings.
diagram.question: A student uses iron to find the percentage of oxygen in air. The volume of air in the flask and tube is **{f} cm³**. The syringe reads **{s} cm³** at the start and **{e} cm³** at the end. Calculate the percentage of oxygen in the air.

items: Air is about 21% oxygen by volume.
A reactive solid removes the oxygen and the gas volume falls.
Include the air in the flask and tube in the starting volume.

blocks.text: Magnesium, hydrogen and sulfur all burn in oxygen. Burning an element in oxygen is oxidation and makes an oxide.

items: Magnesium oxide is an ionic solid.
Hydrogen burns to make water, a liquid.
Sulfur dioxide is a gas with a choking smell.
Magnesium burns with a bright white flame to make white magnesium oxide.
Sulfur burns with a blue flame to make sulfur dioxide.
Hydrogen burns to make water.

blocks.text: Many metal carbonates break down when heated and give off carbon dioxide.

items.meaning: A compound breaks down into simpler substances when it is heated.

items: Copper(II) carbonate changes from green to black.
It makes black copper(II) oxide and carbon dioxide: CuCO₃ → CuO + CO₂.
A Group 2 carbonate decomposes in the same way: XCO₃ → XO + CO₂.
Carbon dioxide turns limewater milky.
The solid loses mass because the carbon dioxide escapes.
Heat to constant mass to be sure that the reaction is complete.
A lid on the crucible stops solid spitting out, but it also stops the gas escaping easily.
Many metal carbonates decompose when heated to give a metal oxide and carbon dioxide.
Copper(II) carbonate turns from green to black.

checks.q: State the approximate percentage of oxygen in air.
Write the equation for magnesium burning in oxygen.
Describe what you see when copper(II) carbonate is heated and name the gas made.
checks.a: It turns from green to black. Carbon dioxide is made.

worked_example.question: A student uses the reaction between iron and oxygen to find the percentage of oxygen in air. The volume of air in the conical flask and glass tube is 260 cm³. The syringe reading at the start is 90 cm³ and at the end is 22 cm³. Calculate the percentage by volume of oxygen in the air.
answer_points: Total volume at the start = 260 + 90 = 350 cm³.
worked_example.tip: Do not forget to add the volume in the flask and tube to the syringe volume.
